title: OAuth Consent Phishing
overview: Review an OAuth consent audit event for an unverified publisher and durable mailbox access.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and entra sign-in or audit projection fields.

attack.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack.rationale: Risky consent may enable theft or misuse of application access tokens. A consent event alone does not demonstrate token theft.

hypothesis: A grant to an unverified publisher with offline access warrants review for unauthorized delegated access.
evidence: Inspect application ID, granting actor, scope and publisher verification. Confirm whether the grant was approved.
false_positive: Internal development applications can have unverified publishers and planned offline access.
tuning: Join approved applications and reviewed scopes. Flag newly granted scopes even for previously trusted apps.
response: Preserve consent evidence, remove the suspicious grant and review mailbox or API activity tied to the app.
prevention: Require administrator review for sensitive consent and audit privileged delegated scopes.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The grant can precede token abuse. The fixture contains no token value or evidence of data access.

options: The order of the UI columns
questions.explanation: Offline access can permit session continuation after initial consent, subject to the provider.

questions.prompt: What should be preserved before revocation?
options: App ID and the grant audit record
questions.explanation: An application identifier and audit record support scoping without retaining credentials.
